description: What a beat can do (beats[].do[].do). at is seconds from the beat's start (default 0). target names an object id; "camera" moves the camera.

show.description: Make a hidden object appear (scales up from nothing).

hide.description: Shrink an object away and hide it.

pop.description: Pop an object in with an overshoot and a sound (numbers, letters).

params.to: [x, y, z] landing spot (the object's base)

drop.description: Drop an object from above; it bounces and squashes as it lands.

params.target: object id, or <id>#<part> for a named part (offset from its rest pose)
object id (a ball, a wheel, a log)
params.to: [x, y, z] where it rolls to
params.radius: rolling radius in metres (default: the object's pivot height, else half its size)

roll.description: Roll along the floor: glide to `to` and turn by distance / radius about the axis across the path, so it never slides. Give a ball pivot: [0, r, 0] (its centre) so it turns about its middle; its at is then that centre.

params.target: object id, or <id>#<part> for a named part (offset from its rest pose)
params.to: [x, y, z] degrees (or by and axis)
params.by: degrees to turn from where it is about axis (instead of to)
params.axis: x, y (default) or z, with by

params.target: object id, or <id>#<part> for a named part (offset from its rest pose)
params.axis: x, y (default) or z: the Euler component that turns. z keeps the x and y tilt (a tilted globe's #globe part, a wheel facing the camera)
params.ease: default cubicInOut; linear for steady turning

spin.description: Spin whole turns about an axis (default the vertical) and stop where it began.

hop.description: A quick hop up and back down; it adds to position, so a hopping object can also move.

params.to: scale factor (number, default 1.3), or [x, y, z] factors to stretch one way (a water level rising: [1, 2, 1])

grow.description: Scale to a new size and stay.

params.loop: default true for Idle/Dance/Walking/Running, else false
params.then: clip to return to afterwards, default the idle

camera.description: Move the camera (any of position, lookAt, fov).

params.voice: a timbre from catalog/story/tts_voices.json or "narrator", default the speaker's meta.cast voice, else meta.voice
params.caption: true to also show the words as a caption
params.who: the speaker's object id (a critter, a character or a shape with face: true): its mouth moves with the voice (Robo nods his head)
params.pitch: 0.8-1.3 (default 1.1, or the speaker's meta.cast pitch): higher or lower voice; soft moves about 0.6 semitones per 10%
params.speed: 0.8-1.2 (default 1, or the speaker's meta.cast speed): times meta.voiceSpeed
params.at: seconds from the beat start, or "after": start when the beat's previous line ends (its measured clip) plus 0.25 s, so two lines in one beat never overlap
params.tune: a melody for a sung line: note names, one per syllable, with :beats for longer or shorter notes ("G4 G4 G4 D4 E4 E4 D4:2"; "|" bar lines ignored). The voice is chanted on the beat (each syllable placed on its note) and a toy glockenspiel plays each note
params.sing: with tune: true (or 0.3-1, how far) to move the voice itself onto the notes (experimental: PSOLA, tools/lib/tts/psola.mjs)
params.tunePatch: the instrument for tune: glock (default), bell, music_box, toy, pluck_high, flute, glass
params.tuneGain: the melody level, 0-1 (default 0.16, 10-14 dB under the voice)
params.rhythm: with tune: true chants the voice on the tune's beat (experimental, can sound choppy); default false: normal speech, the notes follow its syllables
params.keywords: optional { word: icon name, prop name or keyword options }: a badge pops at the side of the frame as each word is spoken (retention kit)

say.description: Speak a line with Piper TTS; the beat lasts at least as long as the voice. With who, the speaker lip-syncs to the clip's loudness.

params.dur: default the rest of the beat
params.style: title (centre), label (a naming word above the subtitles), count (big numeral, right third), subtitle (bottom, wraps), intertitle (a full-frame silent-movie title card: cream words in a double border on warm black; \n starts a new line), chapter (a chapter title over the scene: badge and big outlined words near the top), default subtitle
params.color: colors.json name for the text (colour lessons), default the style's
params.pos: left, right or top: put the caption there instead of its style's place (a count beside the picture, not over it)

params.gain: 0-1 (required): the bed's level, times the scene's own (0.15: a dip under a freeze; 1: back to normal)

music.description: Ramp the music bed's level inside a scene and hold it until the next music action: dip it for a freeze, a sound cue or a quiet moment, then bring it back with gain 1.

burst.description: Fire a confetti or bubbles object (bubbles rise for dur seconds, default 8).

params.target: object id, or <id>#<part> for a named part (offset from its rest pose)

wiggle.description: A happy side-to-side wiggle that settles back.

params.target: critter id (its head nods) or any object

sleep.description: Close the eyes slowly and stay asleep.

params.target: critter, character or shape with face: true
params.feeling: happy, sad, surprised, angry, worried, sleepy or joyful (a big smile with the eyes shut in happy arcs)

feel.description: Show a feeling: eyebrows, mouth and eyes change and the head tilts (Robo uses his face). Stays until the next feel.

params.target: object id: a shape, letter (with colors: every character blends), number block, critter, prop, stroke, pointer, number line (its beam) or fraction bar or circle (its shaded colour)
params.from: colors.json name: blend only the parts drawn in this colour (after recolor) instead of the main colour; critters and props, or a fraction bar or circle's empty colour (its unshaded parts)

paint.description: Blend the object's main colour to another colour (a leaf turning orange, a describing word changing a balloon). With from, blend the parts drawn in that colour instead (a plant's leaf parts turning brown).

params.rig: lights name (soft_day, studio, moonlight, evening, dusk, dim, overcast...); a rig with its own background (dusk) brings it when background is not given

lights.description: Change the stage's light and colours over time: day to night, a dim theatre, a grey winter sky, sand to snow.

stage.description: Change the stage mid-episode: background, floor, rug, fog and light rig crossfade to another preset, and the old preset's set pieces fade out as the new one's fade in (a later preset's pieces are set_<preset>_<id>).

params.to: time like "3:30"; the hands always go forward
params.minuteHand: false hides the long hand, true shows it

clock.description: Turn a clock's hands to a time, the way a real clock moves.

params.to: [x, y, z] the spot to light

aim.description: Point a lamp at a new spot (a torch sweeping across a wall).

params.points: list of [x, y, z] to travel through
params.face: true turns it toward where it is going

path.description: Travel through points at an even speed (a train along its track, a route on a map, a rocket's arc).

params.target: number_line, fraction_bar, fraction_circle, array, grid or cubes
params.order: items (default, one by one), rows or cols (array, grid), rows or layers (cubes)
params.dur: seconds for the whole build, default about 0.4 s a step (shorter steps for big builds, at most 8)
params.sound: one per step, default pop; false for none

build.description: Show the object and reveal its pieces one by one, with a sound each (count along).

params.to: how many parts are shaded (a whole number up to the piece count); fewer unshades
params.cells: piece numbers (from 1) to shade instead of to: exactly these, one after another; cells from an earlier cells list that are not listed again unshade ([] clears)
params.rect: [row, col, rows, cols] (row and col from 1, row 1 on top): shade a block of a grid or array, like cells listed row by row

shade.description: Shade parts in order (left to right, slices clockwise, cells row by row).

params.target: object id (usually one standing on the line)
params.values: list of values to leap to, in turn
params.arcs: true (default) draws each jump's arc on the line; false leaps without arcs; clear wipes them later

leap.description: Arc from value to value along a number line (skip counting, adding on, fractions), leaving the jump arcs.

clear.description: Wipe the leap arcs drawn on a number line so far (they shrink away); later leaps draw new ones.

draw.description: Show it and draw it from start to end (an arrow grows tip first, a callout runs its leader then pops its card).

open.description: Open or close an angle; the arc and the degrees follow.

params.target: object id, or <id>#<piece> (a slice, a cell, an item)
params.result: correct (a green tick, default) or incorrect (a soft red cross)
params.sound: default ding (correct) or a soft boing (incorrect); false for none

mark.description: A badge with a ring over the target: a green tick for correct, a soft red cross for not quite (never scary).

highlight.description: A soft glowing ring that pulses around the target (look here).

params.sound: one per unit, default pop; false for none
params.count: true: numbers 1, 2, 3... pop beside each unit edge as the dot passes

trace.description: A glowing dot runs round the grid's edge from the top-left corner, lighting one unit edge at a time (perimeter); the lit edge stays.

params.at: what to look at: an object id, [x, y, z] or "ahead" (a number here is the start time; then put what to look at in to)
params.to: what to look at, when at is the start time

look.description: Turn a critter's head (Robo's head) toward an object or a point, eased; it keeps looking there until the next look. Turns are limited to what a neck can do.

params.target: an object id or a list of ids to frame
params.yaw: degrees round the targets, 0 (default) = from the front, 90 = from the right
params.pad: extra margin, 0-2: 0.2 frames a box 20% bigger (default 0)
params.fit: approx (default: positions only, the boxes look uses) or exact: thin shapes (plates, discs, bowls) at their real height and every turn applied (a sign stood up with rotation x 90, a turned number line, cards on a turned group)

shot.description: Frame objects with the camera from their approximate sizes so nothing is cropped at 16:9 with the current fov; children (anything with parent pointing at a target, recursively) and teaching-kit labels count, so a card with its word or a number line with its numbers is framed whole. Later camera moves take over.

params.degrees: how far round (positive: the camera moves to its right)
params.radius: metres, blends from the current distance
params.height: metres above around, blends from the current height

orbit.description: Arc the camera smoothly round a point, starting from where it is and turning to look at the point (a 3D model, the Earth, a volume box).

params.places: whole number: + moves the digits left (x 10 per place), - right (/ 10)

shift.description: Slide a place value chart's digits by powers of ten while the decimal point stays; zeros pop in to hold empty places and leading or trailing zeros drop out.

params.pop: true (default) pops them in; false swaps at once

set.description: Put new digits in a place value chart.

params.words: the phrase ("the big storm", first match, case and punctuation ignored) or [start, end] word numbers from 0
params.clear: true wipes earlier highlights first (alone: just clear)

emphasize.description: Sweep a marker-pen highlight behind a phrase on a text card; it stays until cleared.

params.parent: new parent id, or null for the world
params.part: a named part of the new parent (head, a pan...)
params.to: optional spot in the new parent to glide to

reparent.description: Hand an object to another parent (a hat from one head to another) keeping where it is in the world at that moment; later moves are in the new parent's frame.

params.target: Robo, or a critter or prop with an arm or wing part
params.to: an object id or [x, y, z]
params.arm: left or right (his own); default the side the target is on
params.part: the part to point with (default arm, wing, hand, paw or flipper)
params.look: default true: the head looks there too

point.description: Raise an arm (Robo) or an arm or wing (critters) toward something, hold it and lower it again, looking there.

params.question: the opening question, spoken and captioned (required)
params.behind: the cover object, or a named part of one such as "toy_box#lid" (required)
params.target: the object it hides, hidden until the reveal (required)
params.style: lift (default: rises and floats away), slide (moves aside), tip (tips back) or open (the default for a part: turns it to `open`)
params.open: [x, y, z] degrees the part turns to with style open, default [-100, 0, 0] (a lid hinged at its back)
params.slow: true: a gentle reveal about twice as long, no spin (automatic when meta.audience is babies)
params.reveal: seconds after the question before the reveal, default 0.6
params.answer: optional line said after the reveal
params.badge: default true: a pulsing ? badge while asking
params.shot: default true: push in on the cover, then frame the answer
params.caption: default true

hook.description: Open with a surprise: ask a question, wiggle the cover twice, then take it away and pop the hidden answer with a sparkle (peekaboo). Put it in the first beat; the beat stretches to fit.

params.timer: a timer_ring id (default an automatic one at the top right)
params.caption: default true

challenge.description: Point before the timer rings: the prompt is spoken, then the options pulse while a timer ring drains with 3-2-1 ticks, then the answer is celebrated. The beat stretches to fit.

params.answer: the response, spoken after the pause (required)
params.cue: ear, hand (default), mouth, eye or question
params.reveal: optional object to pop (if hidden) or glow with the answer
params.caption: default true

call.description: Call-and-response: a prompt, a pause with a pulsing cue badge (the music dips), then the answer is revealed. The beat stretches to fit.

params.target: a timer_ring id (optional: default an automatic ring at the top right)
params.count: countdown numbers at the end, 0-5, default 3
params.sound: tick per number, default timer_tick; false for none
params.chime: end sound, default timer_chime; false for none
params.keep: true leaves the ring on screen

timer.description: Pop a timer ring in and drain it over dur seconds, with big 3-2-1 numbers and ticks at the end and a chime when it rings.

params.style: pulse (default: grow and glow in turn) or blink (glows flash together)

options.description: Make the answer choices pulse or blink so children know what to choose from.

params.hint: with wrong: the right option, which then glows
params.confetti: with correct: a confetti id to burst
params.sound: default ding (correct) or wrong_soft; false for none

answer.description: Show a result: correct gets a green tick, a gold glow, a happy hop and a ding; wrong gets a soft shake, a gentle cross and a low boop, then the hint glows. Never scary.

params.word: the key word (for the lints and the reader)
params.icon: a badge icon (ear, hand, mouth, eye, question, star, check, heart, drop, sun, leaf, apple, music, home, moon, snow)
params.model: a catalog prop shown in 3D on the badge
params.sound: default per icon; false for none
params.avoid: an object to keep clear of (default the camera's look point)

keyword.description: Pop a keyword badge with a sound at the side of the frame, away from what is being taught (say keywords does this per word).

params.step: a number (fill up to it; the surprise is slots + 1) or next (default)
params.tease: true wiggles and sparkles the surprise slot without filling it
params.sound: default pop per fill, train_whistle when a train is full, magic_sparkle on the surprise; false for none

progress.description: Fill a progress tracker to the next step (or a given one), or tease its surprise slot.
